newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asian traders see LME metals down, except for zinc.
newsitem.headline: Asian traders see LME metals down, except for zinc.

text.p: Base metals prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) are likely to slide on Wednesday, except for zinc which is recovering after last week's fall, Asian traders said.
"On the aluminium market, we've seem quite a lot of selling, possibly long-liquidation, during Asian hours," said a trader at one of Japan's major trading houses.
"We also have options declaration today. It might see a dip towards $1,710. It looks overbought in the short term."
By 0510 GMT, three month aluminium was quoted at $1,725/$1,728, unchanged from 1800 GMT on Tuesday but up slightly from the kerb close at $1,721.
Lead was $606/$609, up from Tuesday's kerb close at $605 and an intra-day low of $603, the weakest since June 1995.

Martin Squires at Rudolf Wolff said in his daily comment: "The new lows have attracted fresh trade interest... However, with the technical indicators trending down in confirmation of the break, expect further underlying tests."
Zinc was at $1,497/$1,501, compared with the kerb close of $1,498. Copper was $2,300/$2,305, compared with $2,307/$2,310 at 1800 GMT on Tuesday and the kerb close at $2,285.

"Zinc still looks strong after last week's sharp fall, although the recovery has been slow," said one trader. "The next key is whether it will breach $1,525 this week or next week. If that happens, it is very strong."

Of the flagship copper, which has taken a backseat over the last several days to zinc and aluminium which have stolen the limelight, traders remained cautious, with support next seen at $2,275, the low on Tuesday.
